content:
Dating reality shows have always been a popular genre, but Apple TV+ has never ventured into this space. Although its newly announced series "The Last Person on Earth" is positioned as a "documentary series" rather than a "reality show," it is still the streaming platform's first dating show.

"The Last Person on Earth" is hosted by renowned relationship therapist Esther Perel and is described as an "innovative experiment."

Esther Perel is a famous relationship therapist and New York Times bestselling author who specializes in studying relationships between people.

Perel is also the central figure of Apple TV+'s newly announced eight-episode dating documentary series "The Last Person on Earth."

The press release states: "In the show, seemingly mismatched participants will be carefully matched by Perel and a team of matching experts and therapists, then sent to the world's most romantic and remote travel destinations to embark on a journey."

It sounds very much like a reality show, but without the negative baggage that comes with the "reality" brand. I suspect Apple is trying to create a more "high-end" image for the dating show genre, hence labeling it as a "documentary series."

The series has not yet announced a premiere date and is expected to debut in 2027.

Speaking of which, Apple also announced yesterday that it will adapt bestselling novelist Rebecca Yarros's latest romance novel into a TV series. It's clear that the streaming platform is working hard to move beyond its existing core genres of sci-fi, comedy, and thrillers to venture into new territory.

Apple TV+ costs $12.99 per month, with discount offers available through the Apple One bundle subscription.
